1) The adjudication to “neutral aromatic” is plausible given extremely small torsional response (E31; absolute delta_dihedral ≈0.09°) and low combined relaxation score (E37), but the argument leans heavily on “no twist” while underusing other available electronic/CT-relevant signals (notably the sizable permanent dipole change S0→S1 in features_summary, which is not promoted into an evidence_id and therefore never weighed explicitly).
2) The emission shift evidence is correctly characterized as small/flat (E72), but “small peak shift” alone is weakly diagnostic between LE/neutral-aromatic vs ICT/TICT because packing/polar microenvironment changes can also yield small shifts without mechanism switching; the absence of bandshape/shoulder information limits how strongly E72 can support a specific label.
3) The writeup treats “electronic redistribution summary is medium” (E36) as generic context, but it could materially affect the neutral-aromatic vs ICT boundary. At minimum, the rationale should explicitly reconcile why a strong gap decrease bucket (E32/E36) does not push toward ICT in the allowed label set.

5) There is an internal feature-bucketing tension: the same torsion change is described as bucket “none” in atb_trends_self notes vs bucket “low” in the structural relaxation profile (E31/E37). This doesn’t change the conclusion (both imply tiny torsion), but it signals that thresholds/axes are being mixed and should be clarified to prevent downstream miscalibration.
